current_answer: As of 4 October 2026, reviewed public evidence does not establish a broad decline across popular deployed models or a confirmed Opus 5.5 capability regression. BridgeBench still shows its latest Opus 5.5 test, dated 2 October, at 94.2% of launch “power,” inside its stated 90–110% range; the composite combines task score, tokens, and cost, and its actual tasks and weights remain private. LiveNerf reports that its 10-day baseline is complete (10 of 30 daily collections as of 3 October), but no post-baseline comparison is available; the first possible call is around 24 October and its 78-item Claude Code subscription test has limited sensitivity. Marginlab also says its new Opus 5.5/high baseline is still being collected and degradation detection is paused, so its displayed rates are not a validated Opus 5.5 before/after comparison. OpenAI and Anthropic reported all systems operational at the 4 October status check. If a familiar task fails, check its product surface and status, save the task and settings, then replay it after recovery against your own baseline before switching.

catalogue_card.question: Does Opus 5.5 have a confirmed decline?
catalogue_card.text: Not from the evidence checked. LiveNerf has finished its baseline but has no post-baseline comparison; its first possible decision is around 24 October. Its test covers one Claude Code subscription path, not every model or user task.

summary: No reviewed public evidence establishes broad capability decline across popular deployed models or a confirmed Opus 5.5 regression.

BridgeBench still shows a 2 October Opus 5.5 result of 94.2% of launch “power,” inside its stated 90–110% range. The score combines performance, tokens, and cost; its task set and weights are private.
LiveNerf reports its 10-day baseline complete after 10/30 daily collections; no post-baseline result is available. The first possible decision is around 24 October.
LiveNerf estimates it can detect about a 7.5 percentage-point shift over a 10-day window. Its validation could not distinguish Opus 5 from Opus 5.5 at 99%.

Marginlab says its new Opus 5.5/high baseline is still collecting and degradation detection is paused. Its page also displays daily and rolling rates plus a +8.5% 30-day label but does not explain their relation to the baseline; do not read these as a clean Opus 5.5 comparison.
OpenAI and Anthropic reported their listed systems operational at the 4 October check. Status does not measure answer quality.
If a familiar task fails, check the product surface and status, save the task and settings, and replay it after recovery against a saved baseline before switching.
uncertainty: BridgeBench’s 94.2% is a composite, not a capability-only score; its actual task set, weights, sample count, and uncertainty are not public.

LiveNerf has completed only the baseline window. Its fixed 78-item panel targets about a 7.5 percentage-point accuracy change per 10-day window; its validation did not distinguish an Opus 5 replacement from Opus 5.5 at 99%, so smaller or different changes may escape detection.
Marginlab says its Opus 5.5/high baseline is still collecting and that degradation detection is paused. The page also reports rates, but does not supply a post-baseline Opus 5.5 comparison.
Provider status is aggregate. It does not establish account-level availability or answer quality.
There is no broad, repeated, representative user-task series across popular models, no first-party pool analytics, and no controlled audience or purchase evidence.
freshness_note: Checked 4 October 2026 at 12:06 UTC. LiveNerf completed its 10-day baseline but has no post-baseline comparison; BridgeBench’s latest displayed Opus 5.5 test remains dated 2 October.
